newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Fujimori to meet at White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Fujimori to meet at White House.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori will meet U.S. President Bill Clinton at the White House on Monday, White House and Peruvian officials said.
The Peruvian leader is extending his stay in Washington until Tuesday, a Peruvian embassy official said, instead of returning to Lima Monday evening.

White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said the meeting, expected to last 30 minutes, would be a "good exchange of views" on the talks between Fujimori and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Fujimori was originally scheduled to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, and not the president, at an early-morning meeting but that was cancelled. She will attend the White House meeting with Clinton.

Fujimori arrived in Washington on Saturday from Toronto, where he held an emergency summit with Hashimoto to discuss what to do about rebels holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

The two leaders agreed to push for direct talks with the rebels, who have held the Japanese residence since Dec. 17., but ruled out the guerrillas' demand for the liberation of about 400 MRTA members jailed in Peru.

Fujimori said on Saturday he was optimistic about talks because the rebels had "implicitly" given ground on their main demand. But the international spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels said Fujimori's interpretation that release of jailed comrades was no longer a key demand was incorrect.
